transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-05 15:00 UTC | Duration ~62 min | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramirez (Redwood CSM); Jordan Blake (CedarPoint Sec Lead), Priya Nair (GRC), Samir Patel (Platform), Leah Ortiz (Legal), Tom Wu (DevOps)

00:00 Alex: ok everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through your SOC 2 / ISO posture and make sure the artifacts we have line up with your control mapping. Is that right Jordan?
00:09 Jordan: yeah, thanks Alex. We're in a bit of a crunch — board asked for a readiness summary. Primary ask is: can Redwood provide attestation artifacts and let our auditors verify controls mapping, and second, how do you handle audit logs and KMS.
00:22 Alex: absolutely, quick agenda: share the reports we can provide, walk through trust center access, RBAC/SSO, then Maya will deep-dive into KMS and log exports.
00:31 Priya: quick note, we need both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Prefer PDFs and an Excel control matrix that maps to our internal clauses.
00:42 Maya: understood. We have a control_matrix_v2.xlsx that maps Redwood controls to common SOC2/ISO clauses — I can send that after the call.
00:49 Tom: also data residency — CedarPoint can't have EU PII leave EU regions for certain workloads. Is that supported?
00:56 Alex: yes, we have private deployment options and region pinning. For hosted customers we can route to specific regions; for strict residency you can run Redwood Private in your VPC or in a cloud region you specify.
01:08 Samir: what's the difference between customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed? Specifically key rotation and access to keys.
01:16 Maya: good question. With customer-managed KMS you manage keys in your cloud KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Redwood can be configured to use your key for data-at-rest encryption; you keep key control and rotation. With Redwood-managed keys we handle rotation but we offer audit logs and attestations. There's trade-offs for ops burden vs control.
01:37 Jordan: do you support HSM-backed keys or BYOK? We need hardware-backed keys for some scopes.
01:44 Maya: yes, we support HSM-backed keys via customer-managed KMS and BYOK flows. There are a couple of integration patterns — I'll diagram the flows and include HSM notes.
01:55 Leah: legal wants to confirm whether Redwood can produce signed SOC2 and ISO reports, and whether auditors can get read-access to evidence in the Trust Center.
02:03 Alex: we publish SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation PDFs. For auditor access, we can provision read-only Trust Center accounts scoped to evidence artifacts. We do SAML SSO provisioning to map to your IdP and RBAC.
02:18 Priya: SSO mapping is important — we need RBAC that separates reviewer access from admin access. Can you map groups from Okta?
02:26 Maya: yes, we map SAML groups to roles in the Trust Center. You'll be able to map omitting italics — sorry, sorry — you'll be able to map Okta groups to reviewer/admin roles. There are default roles: viewer, auditor, admin.
02:42 Jordan: what about audit logs? How long are logs retained and what's the export format? We need at least 12 months retention and ability to export to our SIEM.
02:51 Alex: default retention in hosted is 180 days for token-level request logs, but we have longer retention tiers as an add-on. For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention; we can push logs to S3 or to your SIEM using secure transfer. Exports are JSON newline-delimited with timestamps and request metadata.
03:12 Tom: can we get a sample export? I'd like to test ingestion into Splunk.
03:17 Maya: yes, I'll attach a sample audit_log_export.json and an ingestion guide.
03:24 Jordan: also need assurance that logs are tamper-evident. How do you prevent log alteration?
03:30 Maya: logs are write-once in our audit store and we provide cryptographic checksums and signed export bundles for handoff. For Private you can optionally route logs to an immutable customer-controlled bucket.
03:46 Priya: on the control matrix, we need to see mapping to specific SOC 2 CC controls and ISO 27001 Annex A controls. Will yours be granular?
03:55 Alex: yes, the matrix shows control, description, evidence artifact, location (Trust Center path), and frequency. Example row: CC6.1 - logical access reviews - evidence: access_review_2026Q2.pdf - path: /trust-center/evidence/access-reviews/.
04:12 Jordan: would you be able to show a live path in Trust Center or is that a demo later?
04:18 Alex: for this call we'll share screenshots and a short video walkthrough. For auditors we can provision temporary read-only accounts. Diego: adding — CSM can coordinate auditor onboarding.
04:31 Diego: yep I'll handle the onboarding checklist once we have the access list.
04:37 Samir: regarding private deployment — what's the timeline and what infra do you need from our side?
04:43 Maya: typical Private deployment is 4-6 weeks for small pilot; we need network peering, firewall rules, KMS access (if using BYOK), and IAM roles. We'll provide an infra checklist. For strict residency it's recommended.
04:58 Priya: any known gaps between Redwood's controls and ISO 27001 that we should be aware of?
05:04 Alex: the matrix will call out residual gaps — usually around customer-side controls (like internal HR background checks) that we can't provide. We'll flag those as 'customer responsibility'.
05:15 Jordan: are there examples of previous auditor requests and typical turnaround for evidence?
05:20 Alex: auditors usually request PDFs, system logs, and export bundles; turnaround for most artifacts is 24-48 hours once access is granted. For deep infra logs we may need SE help — Maya to coordinate.
05:35 Leah: legal question — does Redwood allow subprocessor disclosures and where are they listed?
05:40 Alex: yes, subprocessors are listed in the Trust Center under legal > subprocessors. We maintain a public list and provide notifications for changes.
05:50 Tom: ok, small nit: are transcripts of API calls preserved, like prompt/response content? We treat prompts as customer data — retention policy?
05:59 Maya: content retention is configurable. By default, hosted API does not retain prompts beyond short-term telemetry, but we have strong options for opting out. For Dedicated/Private the default is no retention unless you enable logging. We'll include a data-flow diagram.
06:18 Jordan: what about pen tests and vuln scans — do you provide reports?
06:22 Alex: we run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual pen tests; executive summaries are in the Trust Center, full reports can be shared under NDA.
06:32 Priya: ok for our auditors we need the Type II testing period dates — is that listed on the report header?
06:36 Alex: yes, SOC2 reports include period covered and testing dates; ISO certificate includes scope and date issued.
06:45 Jordan: one more question on RBAC: can we restrict who from our org can request data exports? Need approval workflow.
06:52 Maya: currently we have role-based restrictions plus an approval flow for sensitive export requests — for private deployments we can add custom approval hooks using webhooks to your ticketing system.
07:05 Samir: technical follow-ups: how do you authenticate to KMS when running in our VPC?
07:11 Maya: we use short-lived credentials and assume-role patterns; we support KMS grants and IAM roles; we'll show the sample TF module.
07:20 Jordan: ok that's helpful. Could we have a quick walkthrough of which artifacts you'll share now?
07:26 Alex: sure — I'll send SOC2 Type II PDF, ISO 27001 certificate, control_matrix_v2.xlsx, sample audit_log_export.json, and a Trust Center screencap pack.
07:36 Leah: and please include the NDA link for full pen test reports.
07:40 Alex: will do.
07:43 Diego: I'll set up Trust Center accounts for Jordan and Priya as read-only — Jordan, please confirm the email addresses after.
07:51 Jordan: will do.
07:54 Priya: timeline-wise, we want to be able to show a readiness snapshot to auditors by 2026-10-20 — is that feasible?
08:03 Alex: yes if we get the in-scope asset list and access list quickly we can support that. The in-scope list is the gating item.
08:12 Samir: I'll put that together and include residency flags.
08:16 Jordan: one open risk — we may need HSM / BYOK for certain endpoints; if that's a blocker, timeline could slip.
08:24 Maya: we'll prioritize the KMS deep-dive early so we can validate BYOK flow.
08:30 Alex: final recap: Redwood to send artifacts (Alex), SE deep-dive on KMS & logs (Maya), CSM to provision Trust Center read-only accounts (Diego). Action items captured. Anything else?
08:44 Leah: legal will review the SOC2 and check exceptions.
08:47 Jordan: thanks everyone — let's reconvene after the KMS deep dive.
08:52 Alex: great, talk soon.

[call ends] Note: transcription has occasional mis-heard words and speaker overlaps.
